title: The 80-Year Bet: Why Naveen Rao Is Rebuilding the Computer from Scratch

reader_summary.headline: Naveen Rao wants to rebuild computers from scratch to fix AI energy waste.
reader_summary.overview: Naveen Rao argues that current digital computers waste too much energy for artificial intelligence. He believes brains use natural physics efficiently, unlike precise digital math. His new company plans to build analog chips that mimic this efficiency to power future AI.

key_points.text: Digital computers waste energy because they use precise math for fuzzy brain-like tasks.
key_points.evidence_quote: The neural network is actually a stochastic machine. And so why are we using the substrate that is highly precise and deterministic for something that's actually soastic and distributed in nature?

key_points.text: Current AI data centers consume 4% of the entire US power grid.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our AI data centers now consume 4% of the entire US power grid, and we need 400 more gigawatts in the next decade just to keep up.

key_points.text: He believes changing the computer itself is necessary to make artificial intelligence work for everyone.
key_points.evidence_quote: The only way we're going to get to ubiquity is we have to change the computer. The current paradigm is good as it is and as far as it's taken us is not going to take us to that level.

notes: Naveen Rao is cofounder and CEO of Unconventional AI, an AI chip startup building analog computing systems designed specifically for intelligence. Previously, Naveen led AI at Databricks and founded two successful companies: Mosaic (cloud computing) and Nervana (AI accelerators, acquired by Intel). In this episode, a16z’s Matt Bornstein sits down with Naveen at NeurIPS to discuss why 80 years of digital computing may be the wrong substrate for AI, how the brain runs on 20 watts while data centers consume 4% of the US energy grid, the physics of causality and what it might mean for AGI, and why now is the moment to take this unconventional bet.
